analysis: Reviewed the visible portions of provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxSetupTests.swift. The PR change in this file is test-only: SandboxSetupFlow initializers in tests (head lines 539, 550, 669, 813, 835, 866, 901, and later) gain a `waitlist: .approved` argument. This implies production SandboxSetupFlow gained a waitlist dependency/parameter (likely an injectable waitlist check). That production code is not in this batch. No production code was changed or visible here, so I cannot verify default behavior. Test-only code does not add runtime attack surface. The existing tests still assert the security-relevant TB-013/T-061 behaviors: install.sh is fetched only over https, with no userinfo, query or fragment, and redirects are refused. A response over 1 MiB is refused and the script must start with a shell shebang. The staged script is owner-only (0700 directory, 0600 file), and setup never passes the installer's --force. Without a prompt, setup applies only a plan that adds slots. Open question for integration: whether the production SandboxSetupFlow default for the new `waitlist` parameter is a real server-backed check that fails closed. It must not default to `.approved`, a test-only bypass, in release builds. The test patch excerpt is truncated and the head-side text was not supplied. Tests after line ~906 were not visible. No finding is warranted from the supplied evidence. Recommend a check of the production SandboxSetupFlow and the waitlist type in the sibling files, which are outside this unit.
